## Overview

Adds a tensor-descriptor (TD) path to `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` for grouped `int4_w4a16` weights, mirroring the one [#42436](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42436) added to `fused_moe_kernel` (RFC [#42545](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42545)). A is gathered with `tensor_descriptor.gather`; packed int4 B is loaded as bytes and unpacked with `tl.interleave`. `int8_w8a16` keeps the pointer path.

## Claims

- **When TD runs:** `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` resolves on (unset: XPU only; `1`: also CUDA sm100+) and the launch reaches the Triton WNA16 kernel. On XPU that needs `--moe-backend triton`, since default serving picks `XPUExpertsWNA16`. sm90 and ROCm always use the pointer path.
- **Fallbacks to the pointer path:**
  - `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: TD and pointer may round differently, so all batch sizes stay on one path.
  - `BLOCK_SIZE_M < 8`: the `gather()` minimum.
  - `BLOCK_SIZE_M == 32`: TD is −42% there on Arc Pro B60. Not measured elsewhere, so this applies on every device.
  - A single-token batch, in both GEMMs: the down projection now receives the layer's token count as `num_input_tokens`, because its A has tokens × top_k rows.
  - `K % BLOCK_SIZE_K != 0` (with a one-time warning, like `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`).
  - `BLOCK_SIZE_K < 32`: the packed-byte descriptor needs a 16-byte inner block.
- **Kernel speed:** Arc Pro B60 +13…+17% at M 2–20 and +28…+31% at M 41–4096; Arc Pro B70 +10…+13% at M 4–16 but −4.8% at M 2. Pointer path at M 1 and 21–40.
- **E2E (B70):** prefill-heavy +10–11% for both models and Qwen3-30B mc4 +6.0%. Single-stream decode no longer regresses (+0.8%, was −3.6%). Qwen1.5 mc4 is −1.6% (see Validation). The pointer path matches `main` within 0.7%.
- **Accuracy:** gsm8k differences are within the A/A spread. That rules out a drop larger than about 1.5–2 points, not every drop.

## Validation

Unit: `pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "wn16 or wna16"`

| | passed | skipped | failed | tree |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intel Arc Pro B60 (IGC 2.38.2 / compute-runtime 26.27, triton 3.8.0) | 608 | 0 | 0 | this head |
| NVIDIA B200 (sm100) | 480 | 128 (shapes `fused_experts` routes to the CUDA WNA16 kernel) | 0 | this head |
| NVIDIA H200 NVL (sm90, no TD) | 406 | 202 (TD legs) | 0 | this head |

`main` passes the same 384 pre-existing cases on B200 and H200 NVL (CI post-merge image of the base commit).

- `test_fused_moe_wn16`: a `use_td` leg compares TD against the pointer path (tolerance about 6 bf16 ULP at the output magnitude) and the reference. A launch spy asserts which path each GEMM ran.
- `test_triton_wna16_experts_td`: the `--moe-backend triton` route (`TritonWNA16Experts.apply`) with its default config, including BLOCK_SIZE_M 8/16. It asserts no TD in either GEMM for one token.
- `test_fused_moe_wn16_td_forced_config`: forced BLOCK_SIZE_M=8 and an N-tail config.
- `test_wna16_triton_launcher_td_gate`: the fallback decisions, using a fake kernel. On B60, reverting the token gate to launch rows fails its down-projection case and the single-token `test_triton_wna16_experts_td` cases (the spy sees TD in the down projection). Dropping the batch-invariance gate fails its three batch-invariant cases.
- The TD tolerance was widened after a B200 TD-vs-pointer failure at the old one (6.1e-5 abs, 8% rel).
- CI: `test_moe.py` runs in the CUDA MoE kernels job (L4), where the TD legs skip. No CI job runs them on XPU or sm100, so the TD path is covered only by the runs above.

Kernel latency, `fused_experts`, `Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-GPTQ-Int4` shapes (E=60, N=1408, K=2048, top-k 4, group 128), default tiles, median of 7 interleaved rounds; positive = TD faster. Pointer-vs-pointer on identical code differs by ≤0.52%.

| tokens M | 1 | 2–20 | 21–40 | 41–4096 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Arc Pro B60 | pointer in both GEMMs (−0.1%, noise) | +13…+17% | pointer (TD was −42%) | +28…+31% |
| Arc Pro B70 | pointer in both GEMMs (−0.0%) | M 2: −4.8%, M 3: +8.0%, M 4–16: +10…+13% | not measured | not measured |
| NVIDIA B200, opt-in, `fused_experts` | CUDA WNA16 kernel | CUDA WNA16 kernel | CUDA WNA16 kernel | M ≥ 128: +57…+80% |

On this head B60 M = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 measured −0.1%, +13.8%, +12.9%, +14.5%, +13.5%, and its pointer path is within 0.7% of `main` at every M; the other B60 columns are from the previous head, whose dispatch is identical for M > 1. The B70 row is this head. On B200 `fused_experts` sends M·top_k/E ≤ 6 (M ≤ 90 here) to the CUDA WNA16 kernel. `TritonWNA16Experts` sends those shapes to this kernel, where TD runs at BLOCK_SIZE_M 8/16. That regime is unit-tested on B200 but not benchmarked.

E2E: `vllm bench sweep serve`, graph mode, random dataset, seed 42. Arms: `main`, this PR with `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0`, `=1`, and `=0` again (A/A). Each arm-rep runs in a fresh container with a fresh Triton cache, 5 reps interleaved. Output tok/s medians; p is an exact two-sided Mann-Whitney test of TD=1 against both TD=0 arms.

This head, Arc Pro B70. `main` is the 2026-10-26 XPU nightly (`00b6c4c565`); the PR arms add this PR's four runtime files to it (same patch as this head).

| model | scenario (in/out tokens, prompts, concurrency) | TD=1 vs TD=0 | A/A | p | TPOT ms TD=0 → TD=1 | PR TD=0 vs `main` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen1.5-MoE GPTQ | batch1 (1024/512, 10, c1) | +0.8% | −0.1% | 0.0007 | 9.22 → 9.22 | −0.0% |
| Qwen1.5-MoE GPTQ | mc4 (1024/1024, 20, c4) | **−1.6%** | −0.1% | 0.0007 | 14.25 → 14.56 | +0.1% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | batch1 | +0.8% | −0.1% | 0.0007 | 14.23 → 14.23 | −0.1% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | mc4 | +6.0% | −0.8% | 0.028 | 18.52 → 17.51 | −0.7% |

- A dispatch probe at graph capture shows both GEMMs on the pointer path for batch size 1 and TD from batch size 2. On the previous head the down projection ran TD at batch size 1, which caused its batch1 −3.6%.
- Qwen1.5 mc4 decodes mostly at 4 tokens, where the B70 kernel benchmark has TD 10.5% faster. The cause of the E2E slowdown is not established.

Previous head `a0b1f2262a`, TD=1 vs TD=0, other scenarios (identical dispatch except single-token steps):

| scenario (in/out tokens, prompts, concurrency) | B70 Qwen1.5-MoE GPTQ | B70 Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | B200 Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill_heavy (4000/200, 30) | +10.4% (A/A +0.3) | +11.4% (A/A +0.8) | +235% (A/A +0.1) |
| decode_heavy (200/2000, 10) | +0.8% (A/A −2.3) | +0.7% (A/A +3.9) | +161% (A/A +5.4) |
| mixed (1024/1024, 20) | +1.8% (A/A −1.2) | +0.7% (A/A +3.5) | +188% (A/A −5.4) |
| mid32 (200/1000, 32, c32) | +1.3% (A/A −0.3) | +0.2% (A/A +1.8) | +179% (A/A −0.0) |
| mc4 | — | — | +1.5% (A/A +0.6) |
| batch1 | — | — | +2.5% (A/A −0.1) |

- The B200 baseline is the Triton pointer path, which `--moe-backend triton` selects. Default CUDA serving does not use it.
- Engine args: `--moe-backend triton --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192`; Qwen1.5 also `--quantization moe_wna16`.
- Attention was Flash Attention in every logged run (dispatch probe and gsm8k; perf server logs were not kept), so the flag did not toggle Triton-attention TD.
- Qwen1.5 GPTQ produces garbage on CUDA in every arm, including pristine `main`, so it has no B200 column.

gsm8k, `lm_eval --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, full test set, flexible extract, previous head:

| | TD=0 | TD=1 | TD=0 repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| B70 Qwen1.5-MoE GPTQ | 0.4602 | 0.4716 | 0.4655 |
| B70 Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | 0.8772 | 0.8711 | 0.8696 |
| B200 Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 | 0.8848 | 0.8802 | 0.8795 |

The B200 first TD=0 arm differs from both later arms (98.9% identical generations between the repeat and TD=1, 45.9% against the first). It ran first, so treat it as a run-order outlier.

All XPU E2E and accuracy runs used IGC 2.34.4 / compute-runtime 26.18. The `main` stack (IGC 2.38.2 / compute-runtime 26.27) crashes int4 Triton MoE at model level, with and without TD (checked on an earlier tree, not on this head). Unit tests ran on 26.27.

## Details

- **Overlap with [#52577](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52577):**
  - #52577 masks the pointer-path B load, which this PR moves under `else:`. The conflict is textual.
  - The `K % BLOCK_SIZE_K` fallback routes ragged-K launches onto that same unmasked load, so #52577 should land first. Whichever lands second keeps its mask.
- **Other open PRs on this launch site:**
  - [#56154](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56154) rewrites it into a warmup dispatcher.
  - [#56788](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56788) and [#57558](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57558) add tuned XPU configs, which use BLOCK_SIZE_M=32 for some shapes. Those launches would stay on the pointer path.
  - No open PR adds TD to this kernel.
- **Allocator:** `set_triton_allocator` is registered as in `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`. [#61583](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61583) reports that XPU never calls it and that registering it can break torch.compile `split_module`. The graph-mode E2E runs above did not hit that.
- **Design:**
  - The B descriptor is built inside the kernel, as in `fused_moe_kernel`'s TD path.
  - [#63820](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63820) builds a host `TensorDescriptor` for fp8 B on sm90 (`USE_TMA_B`), which ignores `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD`. A host descriptor for packed int4 B was not tried.
- **Default on XPU:** RFC #42545 asks for a separate PR to flip a kernel's default. Like #42436, this PR converts the kernel and follows the shared XPU default in one step; `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0` turns it off. Its `envs.py` entry now lists every consumer.
- **Not covered:** TP > 1, EP, int8, AWQ and Quark checkpoints.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

The B200 first TD=0 arm differs from both later arms (98.9% identical generations between the repeat and TD=1, 45.9% against the first). It ran first, so treat it as a run-order outlier.

All XPU E2E and accuracy runs used IGC 2.34.4 / compute-runtime 26.18. The `main` stack (IGC 2.38.2 / compute-runtime 26.27) crashes int4 Triton MoE at model level, with and without TD (checked on an earlier tree, not on this head). Unit tests ran on 26.27.

## Details

- **Overlap with [#52577](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52577):**
  - #52577 masks the pointer-path B load, which this PR moves under `else:`. The conflict is textual.
  - The `K % BLOCK_SIZE_K` fallback routes ragged-K launches onto that same unmasked load, so #52577 should land first. Whichever lands second keeps its mask.
- **Other open PRs on this launch site:**
  - [#56154](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56154) rewrites it into a warmup dispatcher.
  - [#56788](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56788) and [#57558](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57558) add tuned XPU configs, which use BLOCK_SIZE_M=32 for some shapes. Those launches would stay on the pointer path.
  - No open PR adds TD to this kernel.
- **Allocator:** `set_triton_allocator` is registered as in `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`. [#61583](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61583) reports that XPU never calls it and that registering it can break torch.compile `split_module`. The graph-mode E2E runs above did not hit that.
- **Design:**
  - The B descriptor is built inside the kernel, as in `fused_moe_kernel`'s TD path.
  - [#63820](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63820) builds a host `TensorDescriptor` for fp8 B on sm90 (`USE_TMA_B`), which ignores `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD`. A host descriptor for packed int4 B was not tried.
- **Default on XPU:** RFC #42545 asks for a separate PR to flip a kernel's default. Like #42436, this PR converts the kernel and follows the shared XPU default in one step; `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0` turns it off. Its `envs.py` entry now lists every consumer.
- **Not covered:** TP > 1, EP, int8, AWQ and Quark checkpoints.
